content: Diphtheria is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. This bacterium can lead to respiratory infections and skin infections. Individuals with diphtheria can transmit the bacteria to others through respiratory droplets when they cough or sneeze, or through direct contact with infected wounds. Symptoms of respiratory diphtheria include general weakness, fever, a sore throat, and swollen lymph nodes in the neck. A hallmark of the disease is the formation of a thick, grayish coating in the throat or nose, which can obstruct breathing and swallowing. In severe cases, respiratory diphtheria can result in complications such as damage to the heart and nervous system. Skin infections caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae typically present as shallow ulcers or sores and are generally less severe. In high-income countries, childhood vaccination programs have significantly reduced the incidence of diphtheria. However, the disease remains prevalent in regions where vaccination coverage is low or inconsistent. Travelers to areas such as Asia, the South Pacific, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe who are not up to date with their diphtheria vaccinations are at risk of infection. Vaccination is the most effective method of preventing diphtheria. Diphtheria vaccines are typically administered as combination vaccines, which also protect against tetanus and, in some cases, pertussis (whooping cough). For infants and children, the CDC recommends three doses of the DTaP vaccine to establish strong immunity against diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis. These doses are administered at 2 months, 4 months, and 6 months of age. Two booster doses are then recommended at 15–18 months and 4–6 years of age to maintain immunity during early childhood. For preteens, a single dose of the Tdap vaccine is recommended between the ages of 11 and 12 to boost immunity. Teenagers who did not receive the Tdap vaccine during preadolescence should receive a dose at their next healthcare visit. For adults, a Td or Tdap booster shot is recommended every 10 years following their most recent adolescent dose. Adults who have never received the Tdap vaccine should receive one dose, followed by either a Td or Tdap booster every 10 years thereafter.
